title: Underwriting Note on Repeat Theft at HostCover-Protected Listings
content:
Under **Host Damage Protection (HostCover)**, the theft repeat-loss share follows the theft claims on the same plan that the claims team approved in the 24 months before the settlement date, leaving out claims on the same stay, because a listing that has already lost belongings to a guest is expected to lock away or remove portable valuables and electronics before it is let again. With two or more such claims the theft is settled at 75 percent, with exactly one at 90 percent, and with none in full. The percentage applies to the theft loss being settled, before any guest payment or deductible comes off it.

## Counting the earlier thefts

- Only **theft** claims count, and only those the claims team **approved** on the **same HostCover plan**.
- The approval must fall in the **24 months before the settlement date**.
- Claims on the **same stay** as the theft being settled are left out.

| Earlier approved theft claims (other stays, 24 months) | Theft settled at |
|---|---|
| none | in full |
| exactly 1 | 90 percent |
| 2 or more | 75 percent |

## Cases (hypothetical plans)

- One theft claim approved 10 months before the settlement date on another stay of the plan: settled at 90 percent.
- Two theft claims approved on other stays, 5 and 20 months before the settlement date: settled at 75 percent.
- One theft claim approved 30 months before the settlement date: outside the 24 months, so none count and the theft is settled in full.
- An approved pet-damage claim on another stay 3 months before: not a theft claim, so it does not count.
